what: Real 486 hardware and a real display.
why: Every DOS result comes from headless DOSBox Staging 0.83.0 with CWSDPMI. No physical 486DX, VGA card, keyboard controller or monitor has run `FIZZ2.EXE`, and nobody has looked at its mode 13h picture on a screen.
DOSBox runs at `cycles=max`, which hides what the `f64` rules cost on a 486DX. Fizz 1's `m5/bench` and its 486 cycle estimator are the reference tools, and neither has been run against Fizz 2.

what: The Web page in a browser.
why: The WASM module is replayed under Node and Bun by `tools/web-replay.mjs`. The page in `web/`, its keyboard handling and its canvas have not been driven in any browser.

what: The DOS build in a browser.
why: No js-dos or other in-browser DOS run of `FIZZ2.EXE` has been tried.
Nothing in the skeleton makes sound, and audio cannot be checked headless. The score library of the proof of concept is not part of this repository.

what: Bundling the Web build into a launcher.
why: `dist/web` uses relative URLs so a launcher can host it under any path; no launcher has.

what: The GitHub runner, beyond the runs recorded.
why: CI passed on the head commit of each pull request and on the merge commits listed in the evidence tables ({{m.ciGreen}} merged pull requests green on main). A run not listed there has not been seen.

what: Other DPMI hosts and DOS versions.
why: Only CWSDPMI under DOSBox's own DOS. FreeDOS, MS-DOS, EMM386 and HDPMI are untried, and the FreeDOS-bootable floppy has not been built.
